title: Baleen: ML Admission and Prefetching for Flash Caches
note: ML admission plus prefetching policy for flash caches, trained and evaluated entirely offline on released Meta traces from seven clusters (traces and code at https://www.pdl.cmu.edu/CILES/). Simulation-only, CPU-bound, no root and no flash hardware needed; the A5000 is optional for model training. Ideal single-machine improvement target - policy, the "episodes" residency model, and the Disk-head Time objective are all swappable.
reason: Flash-cache admission and prefetching evaluated entirely offline on released Meta traces; policy, residency model, and objective function are all swappable — an anchor-grade fit.

title: Kosmo: Efficient Online Miss Ratio Curve Generation for Eviction Policy Evaluation
note: Pure trace-driven MRC generation for non-inclusive eviction policies (LFU, FIFO, 2Q, LRFU). Rust binaries, public cache traces (Twitter cache-trace, 52 traces), no privileged access and no special hardware. Artifact also archived at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10569925. Only concern is trace download size against the ~257 GB free on /home, which is manageable by subsetting traces.
reason: S3-FIFO-class target: trace-driven MRC generation for eviction policies, Rust artifact on Zenodo, public Twitter traces, no privilege needs, and adding policies or better sampling is a clean incremental hypothesis.

title: Demystifying and Improving Lazy Promotion in Cache Eviction
note: Trace-driven benchmark and improvement of five lazy-promotion cache eviction strategies plus two new algorithms; the archetypal cache-policy paper for this course and runs on libCacheSim traces
reason: Archetypal cache-eviction study on libCacheSim traces from the cacheMon group: CPU-only, policy swaps are natural testable hypotheses.

title: SIEVE is Simpler than LRU: an Efficient Turn-Key Eviction Algorithm for Web Caches
note: Cache eviction algorithm evaluated on 1559 open traces with a CPU-only user-space simulator (libCacheSim) plus patches to five production cache libraries; no root, no GPU, no network. Strongest fit of this venue-year. Concerns: the full trace corpus is large relative to 257 GB free disk so a subset is needed; throughput/scalability claims were made with 16 threads which matches this machine.
reason: CPU-only libCacheSim eviction study on 1559 open traces with 16-thread scalability claims that match this machine exactly; only disk for the full corpus needs trimming.

title: 3L-Cache: Low Overhead and Precise Learning-based Eviction Policy for Caches
note: Learning-based cache eviction policy evaluated entirely by trace-driven simulation on top of libCacheSim - user-space C++, CPU only, no root, and the headline metric (CPU overhead vs miss ratio) is exactly the kind of trade-off a 10-week improvement project can attack. Concerns - the paper's 4855-trace corpus is many TB; must subset to a few trace families and argue representativeness.
reason: libCacheSim-based trace-driven eviction policy, CPU-only and root-free, with an explicit overhead/miss-ratio trade-off to attack; only the multi-TB trace corpus needs subsetting.

title: FIFO queues are all you need for cache eviction (S3-FIFO)
note: Pure trace-driven cache-eviction study plus a C implementation in libCacheSim; CPU only, no root, no GPU. Ideal fit for the machine and for an improvement-style hypothesis on eviction policy. Concerns - the 6594-trace corpus across 14 datasets is far larger than 257 GB free so a documented trace subset must be chosen; the throughput/scalability claims were made at 16 threads which the 16-core Threadripper matches well
reason: Anchor paper: trace-driven eviction study plus a C implementation in libCacheSim, CPU-only, with an open-ended policy-improvement space; only trace subsetting for disk is needed.

title: PowerInfer: Fast Large Language Model Serving with a Consumer-grade GPU
note: Designed for exactly this machine class: one consumer/workstation GPU plus CPU, hot/cold neuron-aware GPU-CPU hybrid inference with offloading. llama.cpp-based, user-space build, CUDA 11.8/12.x friendly, no root. 7B-13B models in the sparsity-aware formats fit 24 GB or spill to the 125 GiB host RAM by design. Strongest single candidate.
reason: Hot/cold neuron-aware GPU-CPU hybrid offloading designed for exactly this one-consumer-GPU-plus-large-RAM machine, llama.cpp-based user-space build with a mature repo and obvious policy-tuning hypotheses.

title: Learning-Augmented Heuristics: Simple Yet Smart, Robust and Interpretable Cache Eviction
note: Learned *parameters* for static eviction heuristics (S4-FIFO), with released code, pre-trained model, and libCacheSim + CacheLib implementations; evaluation is pure trace-driven simulation over thousands of public traces - perfect for a machine with no root. See also https://libcachesim.com and arXiv 2608.27975
reason: Cache eviction with released code, pre-trained model, libCacheSim/CacheLib integrations and thousands of public traces; pure trace-driven simulation with an open space of policy and parameter-learning variants.

title: Fairness in Serving Large Language Models
note: Virtual Token Counter fair-queueing scheduler for LLM serving - a scheduling policy layered on a serving engine which is cheap to reproduce and extend on one GPU with small models
reason: A fair-queueing scheduler layered on an LLM serving engine is cheap to reproduce with small models on one GPU and opens a wide space of alternative fairness and preemption policies to test.

title: Prompt Cache: Modular Attention Reuse for Low-Latency Inference
note: Precomputed, reusable attention states for repeated prompt segments - a caching/TTFT problem evaluated on single GPU and even CPU. Small, readable prototype; obvious improvement axes (cache admission/eviction, positional handling). Concern - the schema-based reuse can perturb output quality, so an improvement claim needs an accuracy control.
reason: Attention-state caching for repeated prompt segments is a caching/TTFT problem that runs on a single GPU or even CPU, with a small readable prototype and obvious admission/eviction and positional-handling extensions; accuracy control is needed for any claim.

title: Symbiosis: The Art of Application and Kernel Cache Cooperation
note: Dynamically splits memory between an application cache and the kernel page cache for LevelDB, RocksDB and WiredTiger. Entirely user-space: modified KV stores plus a Python/simpy offline simulator, and memory budgets are enforced with cgroup v2, which env.md delegates to the user slice. No root, no kernel changes, single node. Strong improvement target - the sizing policy is a small, self-contained algorithm.
reason: Splitting memory between app cache and kernel page cache for RocksDB/LevelDB/WiredTiger is core OS caching, fully user space with cgroup v2 budgets plus an offline simulator, and the sizing policy is a small self-contained algorithm to improve.

title: Take Out the TraChe: Maximizing (Tra)nsactional Ca(che) Hit Rate
note: Squarely on-topic: a new cache eviction and prefetching policy (DeToX) driven by transactional dependencies, evaluated with OLTP traces and benchmarks on a single node in user space. Strong fit for a policy-improvement hypothesis with trace-driven replay.
reason: Transaction-aware cache eviction/prefetching policy replayed from OLTP traces in user space - a textbook policy-improvement target close to the S3-FIFO anchor.

title: Latency-Aware Caching with Delayed Hits: From Bursty Traffic to Pipeline Architectures
note: Pipeline of orthogonal cache policies with adaptive memory split, plus latency-aware handling of delayed hits - trace-driven simulation on top of the Caffeine framework, purely CPU and memory bound. Concern - Java build and large public cache traces need disk, both fine here.
reason: Adaptive pipeline of cache policies with delayed-hit handling, trace-driven on Caffeine and purely CPU/memory bound - an ideal policy-swap hypothesis space on this machine.

title: CAPSULE: A Storage Prefetcher Harnessing Spatio-Temporal Locality for Cloud-Scale Workloads
note: Clustering-based storage prefetcher evaluated purely by replaying 729 public block traces - MSR, CloudPhysics, Tencent, Alibaba, Meta. No root, no special hardware; artifact repo is explicitly labelled as the paper artifact. Concern: downloading the full trace corpus may exceed the 257 GB free, so pick a subset
reason: A storage prefetch policy evaluated purely by replaying public block traces with an explicit artifact repo — no root, no special hardware, and prefetch/clustering heuristics are an obvious space of testable policy swaps.

title: ArceKV: Towards Workload-driven LSM-compactions for Key-Value Store Under Dynamic Workloads
note: Workload-driven LSM compaction decision engine implemented on top of RocksDB; a clean single-node storage improvement target
reason: Workload-driven LSM compaction on RocksDB with a public repo: single-node, no root, and the compaction decision engine is an obvious space of policy swaps and new workloads.

title: LRU-C: Parallelizing Database I/Os for Flash SSDs
note: Buffer-pool replacement and I/O parallelisation for flash SSDs; user-space DBMS buffer manager on NVMe, no kernel changes needed
reason: Buffer-pool replacement plus I/O parallelisation on NVMe is core caching and I/O management, needs no kernel changes, has a public repo, and eviction-policy variants are directly testable.

title: Structural Designs Meet Optimality: Exploring Optimized LSM-tree Structures in a Colossal Configuration Space
note: LSM-tree level-capacity and run-count design space built on RocksDB; single-node NVMe; only limit is the 257 GB free disk for very large datasets
reason: LSM level-capacity/run-count design space on RocksDB is textbook storage systems, single-node NVMe, with a large well-defined space of policy variants to test.

title: MorphServe: Efficient and Workload-Aware LLM Serving via Runtime Quantized Layer Swapping and KV Cache Resizing
note: Runtime quantized layer swapping plus pressure-aware KV-cache resizing on Vicuna and Llama models, driven by public Azure and BurstGPT traces which the authors already downscale to fit modest hardware. Single GPU, released code
reason: Runtime KV-cache resizing and quantized layer swapping on 7-13B models with released code and Azure/BurstGPT traces the authors already downscale: single-GPU by design with many swappable policy knobs.

title: ADOC: Automatically Harmonizing Dataflow Between Components in Log-Structured Key-Value Stores for Improved Performance
note: Excellent fit. Pure user-space RocksDB auto-tuning framework that controls write stalls by adjusting thread count and batch size to limit data overflow. Evaluation is single-node RocksDB on NVMe SSDs - exactly the target machine. 16 cores and local NVMe are enough to reproduce the write-stall regimes. Concern: the paper sweeps several device classes (SATA SSD, NVMe SSD, Optane) and we only have NVMe, so device-sensitivity results would have to be narrowed or emulated with cgroup v2 I/O throttling.
reason: Pure user-space RocksDB write-stall auto-tuner on NVMe is the ideal storage target; only the multi-device sensitivity sweep needs narrowing or cgroup-based emulation.

title: Nixie: Efficient, Transparent Temporal Multiplexing for Consumer GPUs
note: Best-matched paper in the venue for this machine: a *user-space system service* that time-multiplexes several near-GPU-memory-filling ML jobs on a **consumer GPU** with "no application or driver changes", plus an MLFQ-style scheduler. Eval repo: https://github.com/XOR-op/nixie-eval . Concern: pinned-host-memory pressure experiments assume a large host RAM budget (we have it)
reason: User-space GPU time-multiplexing service with an MLFQ scheduler, explicitly targeting consumer GPUs with no driver changes, plus a separate eval repo — near-ideal for this machine and full of schedulable policy variants.

title: FlexiCache: Leveraging Temporal Stability of Attention Heads for Efficient KV Cache Management
note: Hierarchical KV-cache manager on top of vLLM that classifies KV heads as stable or unstable and offloads cold pages to host memory; explicitly aimed at cutting GPU memory. Single GPU plus large host RAM is the ideal setup, and there is a Zenodo-archived artifact
reason: Hierarchical KV-cache manager that offloads cold pages to host memory is ideal for one 24 GB GPU plus 125 GiB RAM, with a Zenodo artifact and an obvious space of classification/offload-policy variants.

title: Nemo: A Low-Write-Amplification Cache for Tiny Objects on Log-Structured Flash Devices
note: Set-associative flash-cache design built as a CacheLib module; runs in user space on the local NVMe drives
reason: A CacheLib flash-cache module for tiny objects runs entirely in user space on the local NVMe, and set-associative admission/write-amplification policies are an obvious, well-defined hypothesis space.

title: UniCache: Unifying Prefix Cache Eviction for Heterogeneous LLM Serving Workloads
note: Prefix KV-cache eviction policy for LLM serving. Trace-driven prefix-cache simulator plus a vLLM implementation - both run on one 24 GB GPU with a 7-8B model. Ideal improvement target: swap in a better eviction policy and re-run the simulator
reason: Prefix KV-cache eviction with both a trace-driven simulator and a vLLM implementation on one 24 GB GPU is the ideal shape: swap the eviction policy, re-run the simulator, validate end to end.

title: Kairox: Adaptive GPU-CPU Hybrid LLM Inference via Online Neuron Balancing
note: Textbook fit: a llama.cpp-derived hybrid GPU+CPU engine that dynamically rebalances hot/cold FFN neuron groups between a single GPU and host CPU - 24 GB GPU + 125 GiB RAM + 16 cores is the target hardware class
reason: A llama.cpp-derived engine that rebalances hot/cold FFN neuron groups between one GPU and host CPU targets exactly 24 GB GPU + 125 GiB RAM + 16 cores, and the balancing policy is a clean hypothesis surface.

title: Blox: A Modular Toolkit for Deep Learning Schedulers
note: Explicitly a simulator-plus-toolkit for DL cluster scheduling policies, validated by reproducing prior schedulers from traces. Cluster behaviour is simulated, so no multi-node hardware is needed and new policies are cheap to prototype - a near-ideal 10-week improvement target
reason: A modular scheduler simulator validated by reproducing prior policies from traces needs no cluster hardware and makes new-policy prototyping cheap - close to an ideal 10-week improvement target.

title: NEO: Saving GPU Memory Crisis with CPU Offloading for Online LLM Inference
note: CPU-offloaded attention and KV cache for online LLM inference - explicitly designed for one GPU plus host CPU, evaluated on T4/A10G which are weaker than the A5000, and the 16-core/125 GB host is exactly the regime it targets
reason: CPU-offloaded attention and KV-cache management for online serving is exactly the single-GPU-plus-big-host regime of this machine, evaluated on GPUs weaker than the A5000, with obvious policy knobs (offload split, scheduling) to improve.

title: GL-Cache: Group-level learning for efficient and high-performance caching
note: Excellent fit. A learned cache-eviction policy (group-level learning with XGBoost-style utility models) built on Segcache, evaluated by trace-driven simulation over 118 public block-I/O and CDN traces. Entirely user space, CPU only, no root. Traces (CloudPhysics, Twitter, Wiki/CDN) are public downloads; main cost is disk space for traces, which fits in the ~257 GB free. Strong improvement targets: group formation heuristics, feature set, learning cadence.
reason: Learned group-level eviction evaluated by trace-driven simulation over 118 public traces, entirely CPU and user space, with named improvement axes (group formation, features, learning cadence).

title: Write-Aware Timestamp Tracking: Effective and Efficient Page Replacement for Modern Hardware
note: Write-aware timestamp tracking page-replacement policy in a buffer manager; single-node NVMe, pure user-space C++. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/leanstore/leanstore/tree/WATT .
reason: Buffer-manager page replacement is a textbook OS caching problem, pure user-space C++ on local NVMe in a mature LeanStore branch, and replacement policies are the easiest thing in the world to swap and measure.

title: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
note: Prefix-cache admission and eviction policy for hybrid LLMs - the artifact is a trace-driven Python simulator so the whole evaluation runs on CPU, with the GPU only needed for optional end-to-end checks - ideal project target
reason: Prefix-cache admission and eviction policy delivered as a trace-driven CPU simulator is the ideal course target: no GPU needed, and policy swaps map straight onto testable hypotheses.

title: How Much Can RocksDB Chew? Achieving Near-Zero Write Stalls with Sustainable RocksDB
note: Reframes RocksDB write stalls as a control problem and adds an online RL admission controller; single-node and directly reproducible on NVMe
reason: Write-stall admission control framed as a control problem is core storage-engine resource management, single-node NVMe reproducible as-is, and the RL controller is an obvious, well-defined space for policy alternatives.

title: Pie: A Programmable Serving System for Emerging LLM Applications
note: Decomposes the generation loop into handlers driven by user WebAssembly "inferlets"; all sandboxing is user space and the evaluation model sizes fit one 24 GB GPU. Strong candidate for an improvement project (new KV-cache strategies are the paper's own stated extension point). Concerns - none major; needs a Rust toolchain installed in user space.
reason: User-space wasm-sandboxed LLM serving at model sizes that fit 24 GB, with new KV-cache strategies named by the authors as the extension point; only needs a user-space Rust toolchain.

title: InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management
note: KV-cache offloading to CPU memory with speculative prefetch - designed exactly for one GPU plus large host DRAM. 125 GiB RAM and 24 GB GPU are a good match and no root is needed
reason: KV-cache offloading with speculative prefetch is designed for exactly one GPU plus large host DRAM; 24 GB + 125 GiB and no root needed, with obvious prefetch/eviction policy variants.

title: Virtuoso: Enabling Fast and Accurate Virtual Memory Research via an Imitation-based Operating System Simulation Methodology
note: User-space simulation methodology for virtual-memory research - runs entirely on CPU, no root, and is explicitly built as a research platform to extend
reason: Explicitly a CPU-only, root-free virtual-memory research platform built to be extended - the ideal shape for a 10-week OS improvement project on this machine.

title: VIDUR: A LARGE-SCALE SIMULATION FRAMEWORK FOR LLM INFERENCE
note: LLM-inference simulator + benchmark suite: schedulers, batching policies and parallelism can be studied without a cluster, which is ideal for a one-machine project. Released profiling data avoids needing the original hardware. Concern - validating the simulator against real runs on an A5000 requires re-profiling operators locally; multi-GPU configurations remain simulation-only.
reason: LLM-inference simulator lets schedulers, batching and parallelism be studied without a cluster, with released profiling data; only local re-profiling on the A5000 is needed for validation.

title: LLM-42: Enabling Determinism in LLM Inference with Verified Speculation
note: Scheduling-based determinism for LLM inference using verified speculation instead of batch-invariant kernels. Runs on one GPU with a 7-8B model. Official Microsoft repo referenced from the preprint. One of the strongest candidates on this list for a 10-week improvement project.
reason: Scheduling-based determinism via verified speculation runs on one GPU with a 7-8B model and has an official Microsoft repo; the scheduling/verification trade-off is a rich space of testable variants.

title: Efficient, VRAM-Constrained xLM Inference on Clients
note: Best-matched paper on the list: pipelined sharding for CPU-GPU hybrid inference explicitly under a VRAM budget, built on llama.cpp, with an MLSys26 artifact repo and a Zenodo archive. The A5000 plus 125 GiB host RAM is exactly the target regime
reason: Pipelined CPU-GPU sharding under a VRAM budget on llama.cpp with an MLSys AE repo plus Zenodo archive; the A5000 + 125 GiB host RAM is the exact target regime.

title: Beware of Fragmentation: Scheduling GPU-Sharing Workloads with Fragmentation Gradient Descent
note: scope.md explicitly allows cluster/GPU schedulers "evaluated with simulators or traces": the paper's 6,200-GPU results come from a Go-based Kubernetes scheduler *simulator* replaying public Alibaba traces, which runs as a normal user process on one machine. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: Go must be installed via conda; the real-cluster deployment half of the paper is not reproducible, and simulator-only results weaken an "improvement" claim unless the fragmentation metric itself is the target.
reason: GPU-sharing scheduling policy whose headline results come from a Go simulator replaying public Alibaba traces, with Available+Functional+Reproduced badges - alternative fragmentation metrics are an obvious testable hypothesis.

title: KTransformers: Unleashing the Full Potential of CPU/GPU Hybrid Inference for MoE Models
note: A single-GPU-plus-large-DRAM system by construction - the exact shape of this machine (1x24 GB GPU, 125 GB RAM). The Expert Deferral mechanism and the async CPU-GPU scheduler are hardware-agnostic and directly improvable. Very actively maintained (19.5k stars). Concerns - the headline CPU kernels are Intel AMX-specific and this is an AMD Zen3 Threadripper with no AMX and no AVX-512, so the CPU-side speedups will not reproduce as published; and 671B DeepSeek-V3/R1 needs far more than 125 GB, so a smaller MoE (e.g. Mixtral-class or Qwen3-MoE) scale-down is required.
reason: A single-GPU-plus-large-DRAM offloading system shaped exactly like this machine, with a hardware-agnostic expert-deferral and async scheduler to improve; the AMX-specific CPU kernels will not reproduce on Zen3 and DeepSeek-scale models need a smaller MoE substitute.

title: HotRAP: Hot Record Retention and Promotion for LSM-trees with Tiered Storage
note: RocksDB-based LSM-tree with hot-record promotion on tiered storage; evaluated on one 8-vCPU instance with a fast NVMe plus a slow disk. Concern: the slow tier was AWS gp3 and would have to be emulated on the local NVMe
reason: RocksDB hot-record promotion across storage tiers is textbook OS caching/storage work on a modest 8-vCPU footprint; the promotion policy is a small tunable algorithm, only the slow tier must be emulated locally.

title: Sampling-based Predictive Database Buffer Management
note: Sampling-based predictive buffer replacement evaluated both by simulation on Redshift traces and by patching PostgreSQL; a textbook cache-policy improvement target that fits this machine perfectly
reason: Predictive buffer replacement evaluated both by trace simulation and a PostgreSQL patch is a textbook cache-policy improvement target that fits this machine exactly; the linked repo is only a test-scripts repo so artifact completeness needs checking.

title: Optimizing LLM Queries in Relational Data Analytics Workloads
note: Row and field reordering to maximize KV-cache reuse for batch LLM analytics queries - works against a single-GPU vLLM instance with Llama-3-8B and the win is measured as job completion time - reordering algorithm itself is CPU-side. Merge note: scout linked the subdirectory/branch https://github.com/lynnliu030/artifact-eval/tree/llmsql .
reason: KV-cache-reuse-maximizing request reordering against a single-GPU vLLM with Llama-3-8B is exactly our hardware; the reordering algorithm is CPU-side and swapping in better orderings is a clean testable hypothesis.

title: SLoRA: Scalable Serving of Thousands of LoRA Adapters
note: Unified paged memory pool for adapter weights + KV cache, adapter prefetch from host memory, custom batched-LoRA kernels; the paper explicitly claims single-GPU operation. Strong fit for a memory-management or admission-policy improvement. Concern - tensor-parallel experiments are multi-GPU and must be dropped.
reason: Unified paged memory pool plus adapter prefetch on a single GPU is a memory-management problem with many admission/eviction policy hypotheses; only TP experiments must be dropped.

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?
note: Systematic vLLM-based study of n-gram, EAGLE/EAGLE-3, draft-model and MTP speculative decoding, with a released vLLM fork and simulator - a clean reproduction-or-improve target. Concerns: the study's large-batch and large-model points need more than 24 GB, so the hypothesis must be re-tested at a smaller scale
reason: Released vLLM fork plus simulator make this a clean reproduce-or-improve target; re-testing the speculative-decoding claims at 24 GB scale is itself a strong hypothesis.

title: How Soon is Now? Preloading Images for Virtual Disks with ThinkAhead
note: Data-driven block preloading (prefetch/admission policy) for virtual disk images, evaluated largely by trace-driven simulation; production Alibaba EBS image-boot traces released at https://tianchi.aliyun.com/dataset/216164. Concern: the paper also reports cluster experiments on Alibaba EBS, which cannot be reproduced - only the prediction + simulation half is in reach here.
reason: Prefetch/admission policy for virtual-disk blocks with released Alibaba traces and an AE repo; the simulation half is squarely in reach and policy swaps are obvious hypotheses, only the EBS cluster half is lost.

title: SPADE: Signal-Aware DAG Scheduling and Dynamic Provisioning for Data Processing Clusters
note: Explicitly in-scope form: besides the Spark-on-Kubernetes prototype the authors release a *high-fidelity Spark simulator* driven by Alibaba/TPC-H traces plus carbon/price signals, which runs fine on one CPU-only host. Concern: the 100-node K8s prototype path is out of reach - the simulator is the only usable route. Merge note: the scout's repo-link cell held the PDF URL; the repository given in the scout's prose (https://github.com/umass-solar/adaptive-dag) is used here.
reason: DAG scheduling and provisioning with a released high-fidelity Spark simulator driven by Alibaba/TPC-H traces is exactly the CPU-only scheduling study this machine supports; only the K8s prototype is out of reach.

title: Leveraging Approximate Caching for Faster Retrieval-Augmented Generation
note: Proximity is an LSH-based approximate key-value cache in front of a RAG vector database - squarely a cache admission/eviction/approximation policy study, and the clearest single-node fit in the venue. Rust implementation, MMLU and MedRAG benchmarks, embedding model and a 7-8B generator both fit in 24 GB FP16. Rust is not installed but rustup into $HOME needs no root. Concern: the MedRAG corpus plus index is a multi-tens-of-GB download against ~257 GB free.
reason: An LSH-based approximate cache in front of RAG is a textbook admission/eviction/approximation policy study on one GPU; only risk is a multi-tens-of-GB corpus download and a user-space Rust install.

title: Orion: Interference-aware Fine-grained GPU Sharing for ML Applications
note: Intercepts CUDA kernel launches in user space and schedules operators from co-located clients on one GPU. Single-GPU by design and the whole point is contention on one device. Concern - built against a specific PyTorch/CUDA pairing, so pinning a working toolchain on driver 535 / CUDA 11.8 is the main build risk
reason: Fine-grained GPU sharing by intercepting kernel launches in user space is single-GPU by design and contention-focused, giving many scheduling-policy hypotheses; the pinned PyTorch/CUDA toolchain on driver 535 is the main risk.

title: Simple Is Better: Multiplication May Be All You Need for LLM Request Scheduling
note: A request-router scoring policy (KV-hit indicator x load indicator) - cheap to re-implement and to evaluate against the released Alibaba/Qwen usage traces. Concern: the real setting is several serving instances, so on one GPU it needs small models plus multiple processes, or trace-driven replay of the router only
reason: A simple KV-hit x load router score is cheap to re-implement and re-evaluate against released traces; the multi-instance setting needs small models or trace-driven replay.

title: vAttention: Dynamic Memory Management for Serving LLMs without PagedAttention
note: Contiguous virtual KV cache using CUDA virtual-memory APIs - single-GPU; concern: the finest-granularity variant ships a patched nvidia-uvm kernel module that we cannot load, but the 2 MB-granularity path uses only user-space CUDA APIs
reason: KV-cache memory management on one GPU with a Microsoft repo; the 2 MB-granularity path uses only user-space CUDA VM APIs, and only the finest variant needs the unloadable nvidia-uvm patch.

title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion
note: KV-cache fusion with selective recompute for RAG prefill; vLLM-based prototype runs on one GPU and a 7B FP16 model fits in 24 GB. Concern - some paper configurations use larger models and multiple GPUs, so the study must be scaled down to 7B class models
reason: KV-cache reuse with selective recompute on a vLLM prototype fits a 7B FP16 model in 24 GB, and the recompute-selection heuristic is an obvious tunable.

title: Cache-Centric Multi-Resource Allocation for Storage Services
note: HARE is a cache-size-aware multi-resource (cache/IO/CPU) allocation algorithm - a policy problem that is naturally simulated or run in user space, with public Twitter cache traces. Two prototypes also released: https://github.com/WiscADSL/hopperkv and https://github.com/WiscADSL/bunnyfs. Concerns: BunnyFS issues I/O through SPDK, whose setup (hugepages, VFIO binding) normally needs root; HopperKV caches DynamoDB behind Redis and would need DynamoDB-local or an AWS account. The algorithm itself is the tractable target.
reason: Cache-size-aware multi-resource allocation over public Twitter traces is the archetypal simulatable policy project with three released repos; only the SPDK and DynamoDB prototypes are out of reach, and the algorithm itself invites many policy variants.

title: Virtual-Memory Assisted Buffer Management
note: Buffer pool built on hardware virtual memory - directly a user-space memory-management design and an excellent improvement target. Concern: the second half of the paper (exmap) is a Linux kernel module and cannot be built or loaded without root; only vmcache itself is reproducible here
reason: vmcache is user-space virtual-memory-based buffer management - a textbook OS memory topic with a compact, well-known repo and many eviction/pointer-swizzling variants to test; only the exmap kernel module is out of reach.

title: Prism: Cost-Efficient Multi-LLM Serving via GPU Memory Ballooning
note: Elastic KV-cache memory ballooning across co-served models; the balloon driver (kvcached) is released and actively maintained, and multi-model co-serving on a single 24 GB GPU is the interesting regime. Concern: production evaluation uses many GPUs and bursty multi-model traces
reason: Elastic GPU-memory ballooning across co-served models is exactly the single-24GB-GPU regime, kvcached is released and maintained, and the ballooning policy is a clean hypothesis surface.

title: Jenga: Effective Memory Management for Serving LLM with Heterogeneity
note: An attention-property-aware KV allocator implemented inside vLLM; single-GPU memory-utilization and throughput claims are directly measurable here, and the allocation policy is easy to perturb for an improvement hypothesis. Concerns - several evaluated models (large MoE and multimodal) exceed 24 GB, so the model set must be scaled down; upstream vLLM has moved on, so the AE snapshot may need pinning.
reason: KV-cache allocator inside vLLM is exactly the OS-style memory management this course wants, with a dedicated AE repo and an allocation policy that is trivially perturbable; only the large MoE/multimodal model set needs scaling down.

title: Taming Throughput-Latency Tradeoff in LLM Inference with Sarathi-Serve
note: Chunked-prefill scheduling to trade throughput vs latency in LLM serving - pure user-space Python on top of vLLM. Paper used A100/A40 but a 7B model in FP16 fits the 24 GB A5000 so single-GPU scale-down is natural

note: Code generation for a declarative query language covering both relational and nested JSON workloads including a corrected loop scheduler; compiler and runtime work in user space
reason: Query-language code generation runs comfortably in user space with a linked repo, but compiler work for a declarative DSL is well outside OS resource management.

title: Agents of Autonomy: A Systematic Study of Robotics on Modern Hardware
note: RoWild is an open-source cross-platform user-space robotics benchmark suite (C++/Python, CPU and CUDA) that the paper profiles end-to-end on everything from embedded CPUs to server GPUs; one 16-core CPU plus one A5000 covers the high-end configuration. Concern: the paper is a characterization study and its own conclusions argue for hardware changes, so an improvement project would have to target the software side (kernel fusion, batching, data structures in the motion-planning and SLAM workloads). Second concern: the published characterization leans on architectural counters that perf_event_paranoid=3 blocks, so a reproduction would be limited to wall-clock timing.
reason: RoWild is a clean open user-space benchmark suite, but the paper is a characterization whose own conclusions argue for hardware changes and whose analysis leans on blocked perf counters.

title: Pylo: Towards Accessible Learned Optimizers in PyTorch
note: CUDA-accelerated learned-optimizer kernels exposed through torch.optim; the reported throughput gains are single-GPU ViT-B/16 training numbers. Concern: the large-scale pre-training claims assume more compute than one A5000
reason: CUDA kernels behind torch.optim are single-GPU and the repo looks complete, but learned optimizers are an ML-training-method contribution rather than systems resource management.

title: Is Your Learned Query Optimizer Behaving As You Expect? A Machine Learning Perspective
note: critical re-evaluation of learned query optimizers; released harness makes a careful reproduction straightforward
reason: Released harness makes a careful reproduction straightforward, but learned query optimization is the anchor example of weak OS fit and the paper is already a re-evaluation.

title: Declarative Sub-Operators for Universal Data Processing
note: MLIR-based sub-operator IR and compiler in LingoDB; C++/LLVM builds in user space, CPU-only
reason: MLIR sub-operator compiler with a dedicated reproducibility repo; CPU-only and buildable, but a data-systems compiler rather than an OS topic.

title: SeRF: Segment Graph for Range-Filtering Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: Range-filtering ANN search index; CPU only, single node, modest memory
reason: CPU-only, modest-memory ANN index that runs easily here, but range-filtering vector search is not an OS resource-management problem.

title: Tilus: A Tile-Level GPGPU Programming Language for Low-Precision Computation
note: Tile-level GPGPU DSL for low-precision kernels; Ampere is a supported target. Concern: some tutorials target Blackwell-only features
reason: A GPU kernel DSL/compiler is only systems-adjacent for an OS course; Ampere is supported and the NVIDIA repo is real, but some features target Blackwell.

title: Subspace Collision: An Efficient and Accurate Framework for High-dimensional Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
note: Clustering-based ANN index framework; single machine
reason: ANN index framework runs comfortably on one machine but is an algorithms/data-structures contribution rather than an OS systems-resource problem.

title: FederatedScope: A Flexible Federated Learning Platform for Heterogeneity
note: Event-driven federated learning framework; the standard mode simulates many clients as processes on one node with one GPU
reason: A mature FL platform that simulates clients on one node, but it is framework/ML infrastructure rather than an OS resource-management result to improve.

title: Paralegal: Practical Static Analysis for Privacy Bugs
note: Rust static analyzer (PDG extraction + policy checking); entirely user-space, CPU-only, with a Zenodo artifact DOI and Available + Functional + Reproduced badges. Concerns: needs a pinned Rust nightly toolchain plus rustc internals (installable via rustup into $HOME); the eight evaluated applications are large Rust codebases whose builds are long but single-machine.
reason: Excellent badged artifact and CPU-only, but privacy static analysis is far from OS resource management and the result is fairly closed to incremental systems extension.

title: Removing Obstacles before Breaking Through the Memory Wall: A Close Look at HBM Errors in the Field
note: The artifact ships both the released HBM error dataset and the hierarchical failure-prediction pipeline, so it is a fully trace-driven learned-prediction study that runs on CPU here. Concern: it is a field study, so an improvement has to come from better prediction models or features rather than from a system change
reason: Fully trace-driven with a released dataset and prediction pipeline, but it is a field failure study whose only improvement axis is a better predictor, not a system change.

title: Keep It Simple: Testing Databases via Differential Query Plans
note: Differential-query-plan DBMS testing implemented in SQLancer; runs DBMSs in user space, no root
reason: SQLancer runs root-free and is a mature codebase, but automated bug-finding for DBMSs is explicitly out of the OS-course sweet spot.

title: Bridging the Gap between Relational OLTP and Graph-based OLAP (GART)
note: In-memory user-space system; the core contributions (mutable CSR, coarse-grained MVCC versioning, flexible property store) are data-structure/locality work measurable with wall-clock timing on one node. Code released both as SJTU-IPADS/vegito branch gart (AE link) and the maintained GraphScope/GART. Concerns: depends on the large Vineyard/GraphScope stack; LDBC SNB dataset generation is time-consuming.
reason: Mutable CSR and MVCC layout work is measurable on one node, but it depends on the heavy Vineyard/GraphScope stack and slow LDBC data generation, which will eat much of the 10 weeks.

title: Scalable Model-Based Management of Massive High Frequency Wind Turbine Data with ModelarDB
note: model-based time-series compression evaluation in Rust. Concern: the edge-to-cloud pipeline must be collapsed onto one host
reason: Model-based time-series compression is storage-adjacent and Rust builds in user space, but the edge-to-cloud pipeline must be collapsed onto one host and the repo is an analyzer rather than the full system.

title: Ken: An Execution Engine for Unstructured Database Systems
note: Execution engine that adapts model cascades to query load while managing GPU memory and data movement. Concern: model sizes must be kept within 24 GB
reason: Load-adaptive model cascades with GPU memory management touch resource scheduling, but the repo is a submission snapshot and every model must be trimmed to fit 24 GB.

title: Serving and Optimizing Machine Learning Workflows on Heterogeneous Infrastructures
note: ML-workflow serving and placement optimizer. Concern: original evaluation spans an edge-cloud heterogeneous cluster - on one host it must run as co-located processes or the placement optimizer studied offline from profiles
reason: Workflow placement across an edge-cloud heterogeneous cluster cannot be reproduced faithfully on one host, leaving only the offline optimizer, and the 2023 artifact's state is unknown.

title: Fast, Approximate Vector Queries on Very Large Unstructured Datasets
note: Vector query engine that builds a per-query error-latency profile - the single-worker path is the interesting mechanism and runs in user space - Concern: headline numbers use DEEP1B on four c5.metal instances so experiments must be scaled to SIFT or GIST million-to-100M datasets to fit 125 GiB RAM and 257 GB disk
reason: The per-query error-latency profile is an interesting single-worker mechanism, but the headline numbers use DEEP1B on four c5.metal nodes so everything must be re-scaled, and the domain is ANN search.

title: Unified Static–Dynamic Pruning for Efficient LLM Inference
note: Unified static and dynamic weight pruning with custom CUDA-core and Tensor-Core kernels. Concern: kernels are tuned for newer inference GPUs so Ampere performance must be re-measured
reason: Weight pruning is primarily a model-compression contribution with custom kernels tuned for newer GPUs, so Ampere would require re-measurement before any improvement claim holds.

title: ALCOP: Automatic Load-Compute Pipelining in Deep Learning Compiler for AI-GPUs
note: Compiler-native multi-stage multi-level load-compute pipelining in TVM plus an analytic performance model for schedule search - entirely single-GPU kernel generation - concern - pinned to an older TVM and CUDA and the pipelining depth assumptions target A100 so Ampere consumer retuning is part of the work
reason: Single-GPU compiler pipelining with an analytic cost model would fit, but the artifact is pinned to an older TVM/CUDA and its pipelining depths assume A100, so much of the effort becomes porting.

title: ModelKeeper: Accelerating DNN Training via Automated Training Warmup
note: Training warmup by transforming weights of previously trained models - the matching plus transformation logic is CPU work and warm-started training of small models fits one 24 GB GPU - Concern: the paper uses a large shared cluster and a big model zoo so the zoo and datasets must be scaled down
reason: Warm-start matching and weight transformation are CPU-side and small models fit one GPU, but the paper's value comes from a large cluster and model zoo that must be heavily scaled down.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of GNN Training Systems: A Data Management Perspective
note: systematic evaluation of GNN training systems from a data-management perspective. Concern: distributed configurations must be dropped
reason: A benchmarking harness for GNN training systems gives a ready evaluation platform, but distributed configurations must be dropped and a measurement study leaves an ambiguous improvement target.

title: MiLo: Efficient Quantized MoE Inference with Mixture of Low-Rank Compensators
note: 3-bit MoE quantization with low-rank compensators and Tensor-Core kernels - Ampere supports the INT-based kernels - concern: Mixtral-8x7B at 3 bits is roughly 20 GB so it only just fits 24 GB and calibration-free quantization still needs large host RAM
reason: 3-bit MoE kernels run on Ampere but Mixtral-8x7B at 3 bits only just fits 24 GB and the contribution is mostly quantization accuracy rather than resource management.

title: sMVX: Multi-Variant Execution on Selected Code Paths
note: In-process monitor plus custom loader, entirely user space, no kernel module and no root; repo builds libmonitor.so / liblmvx.so with plain make and evaluates on user-space server applications. Concern: isolation of the monitor relies on Intel MPK. The Threadripper PRO 5955WX is Zen 3, which does expose protection keys, but the pku CPU flag must be confirmed before committing; without it the MPK path would have to be stubbed or emulated.
reason: In-process monitor and custom loader build with plain make and need no root, but isolation depends on MPK whose availability on this Zen 3 part must be confirmed, and the topic is software hardening rather than resource management.

title: Styx: Transactional Stateful Functions on Streaming Dataflows
note: Deterministic transactional runtime for stateful functions on a dataflow engine; concern - normally deployed as a multi-worker cluster, would run as processes on one host
reason: Deterministic transactional dataflow runtime is systems-adjacent but normally a multi-worker cluster; collapsing it to processes on one host weakens the headline throughput claims.

title: R^3: Record-Replay-Retroaction for Database-Backed Applications
note: Record-replay-retroaction runtime for database-backed applications; Java services plus PostgreSQL/VoltDB, all runnable in user space on one host. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/DBOS-project/apiary/tree/r3-exp .
reason: Record-replay runtime for DB-backed apps runs entirely in user space, but it needs a Java + PostgreSQL/VoltDB stack stood up by hand from an experimental branch.

title: Solving Max-Min Fair Resource Allocations Quickly on Large Graphs
note: Fast max-min fair allocators evaluated on WAN traffic engineering and cluster scheduling workloads (public Philly traces); Python plus C# with Gurobi, CPU only, trace-driven. Concerns: needs a Gurobi academic license and .NET installed in user space; the contribution is algorithmic, so an improvement project would be about solver formulations and approximation quality rather than systems engineering.
reason: Trace-driven allocation on public Philly traces fits the machine, but the contribution is algorithmic/solver-centric and requires a Gurobi license plus a user-space .NET install.

title: Optimizing Deep Learning Inference via Global Analysis and Tensor Expressions
note: Inter-operator DNN inference compiler; single NVIDIA GPU evaluation. Concern - artifact is packaged with Docker files that must be reproduced with conda/pip since Docker is unavailable.
reason: Single-GPU inter-operator inference compiler is in scope, but the artifact is Docker-packaged and must be re-created with conda/pip since Docker is unavailable.

title: Metis: Fast Automatic Distributed Training on Heterogeneous GPUs
note: The released component is the CPU-only auto-planner plus cost model and profiler, which can be run and improved on one machine against recorded or synthetic device profiles. Concern: end-to-end validation needs a heterogeneous multi-GPU cluster, so an improvement would have to be argued from the planner and cost model
reason: Only the CPU-only planner and cost model are runnable here; without a heterogeneous multi-GPU cluster any improvement must be argued from planner search quality alone.

title: AdaParse: An Adaptive Parallel PDF Parsing and Resource Scaling Engine
note: Adaptive PDF-parsing and resource-scaling engine for building training corpora - user-space Python parsers plus a learned parser selector - concern: paper scales on an HPC cluster, so single-node runs need a reduced document set
reason: Data-preprocessing pipeline with a learned parser selector is systems-adjacent; HPC-scale evaluation needs a much reduced document set locally.

title: NeutronOrch: Rethinking Sample-based GNN Training under CPU-GPU Heterogeneous Environments
note: CPU-GPU task orchestration for sample-based GNN training
reason: CPU-GPU task orchestration for GNN training is a plausible single-node target, but the thin note leaves artifact completeness and scale unknown.

title: Excalibur: A Virtual Machine for Adaptive Fine-grained JIT-Compiled Query Execution based on VOILA
note: Adaptive fine-grained JIT-compiled query execution VM; C++ single node, LLVM is conda-installable. Concern: research-grade build with heavy dependencies
reason: Adaptive JIT query execution is a runtime contribution that fits one node, but the research-grade LLVM-heavy build is real friction.

title: BladeDISC: Optimizing Dynamic Shape Machine Learning Workloads via Compiler Approach
note: Dynamic-shape ML compiler; single GPU is enough to reproduce most kernels. Concern: large build, CUDA/TF/PyTorch version pinning against driver 535
reason: Dynamic-shape ML compiler is systems-adjacent and single-GPU sufficient, but the build is large with CUDA/TF/PyTorch pinning risk against driver 535.

title: Enabling Transparent Acceleration of Big Data Frameworks using Heterogeneous Hardware
note: Transparent JIT offload of JVM big-data operators to accelerators via TornadoVM; the GPU path works on one A5000 with the NVIDIA OpenCL/PTX backend. Concern: paper also evaluates FPGA, and the Flink part must be run in local mode
reason: JIT offload of JVM operators is runtime/compiler work; the GPU path fits one A5000 but building Flink plus TornadoVM plus a JDK in user space is heavy and the FPGA results are out of reach.

title: Pre-train and Search: Efficient Embedding Table Sharding with Pre-trained Neural Cost Models
note: Learned cost model plus search for DLRM embedding-table sharding - training the cost model and running the search is a single-GPU offline workload driven by the public dlrm_datasets traces - concern - the end-to-end payoff was measured on a production multi-terabyte DLRM so only the benchmark-dataset results are reproducible here
reason: Learned cost model plus search for table placement is a learned-systems component runnable on one GPU, but the headline payoff was a production multi-TB DLRM so only the benchmark slice reproduces.

title: RoleML: a Role-Oriented Programming Model for Customizable Distributed Machine Learning on Edges
note: Python programming model plus runtime; roles are ordinary processes and can be co-located on a single host, and the paper's headline claim is low runtime overhead of the abstraction. Repo is by the first author. Concern: the automatic role-offloading mechanism is built on containerization and Docker/Podman are not installed, so that sub-feature would need porting to plain processes or bwrap.
reason: Roles are plain processes so co-location on one host works and the overhead claim is directly measurable, but the role-offloading feature assumes containers that are not installed and must be ported to bwrap.

title: Optimizing Dynamic Neural Networks with Brainstorm
note: Framework for dynamic (sparsely activated, MoE-style) networks using Cell and Router abstractions plus profile-guided dynamic optimisation; single-GPU inference workloads, and the memory-saving results are attractive on a 24 GB card. Concern: some evaluated models are large MoEs that will need to be scaled down. AE branch: https://github.com/Raphael-Hao/brainstorm/tree/osdi2023ae .
reason: Profile-guided routing for dynamic networks with a dedicated AE branch and attractive memory savings on 24 GB, but several evaluated MoEs need scaling down and the framework is ML-runtime rather than OS.

title: Pilot Execution: Simulating Failure Recovery In Situ for Production Distributed Systems
note: Pure user-space runtime library plus analysis framework that dry-runs recovery actions in distributed systems - target systems (HDFS, ZooKeeper, Kafka class) can be run as multiple processes on one host. Concern - some case studies assume production-scale deployments.
reason: A user-space recovery dry-run runtime is systems-adjacent and runnable as local processes, but some case studies assume production scale and the 2026 repo is unproven.

title: SHiFT: An Efficient, Flexible Search Engine for Transfer Learning
note: Search engine over a pretrained-model zoo with cost models and caching; one A5000 suffices for the small models. Concern: full model zoo plus datasets is a large download
reason: Cost models and caching over a model zoo are systems-adjacent, but the full zoo plus datasets is a large download against ~257 GB free.

title: Enabling Tensor Language Model to Assist in Generating High-Performance Tensor Programs for Deep Learning
note: Language model that emits tensor-program schedules for TVM/Ansor - learned component inside a compiler. Runs on one GPU. Concern - fine-tuning the tensor language model is compute heavy so a scaled-down model or released checkpoints would be needed
reason: A learned component inside a tensor compiler is on the edge of scope and fine-tuning the model is compute-heavy, so the project would depend on released checkpoints.

title: PIT - Optimization of Dynamic Sparse Deep Learning Models via Permutation Invariant Transformation
note: GPU sparse-kernel compiler/runtime for dynamic sparsity; the mechanism is per-GPU and Ampere sm_86 is supported by the CUDA kernels. Concerns - the AE README asks for 8x V100-32GB or 1x A100-80GB and 200-700 GB disk, so models must be scaled down to fit 24 GB and 257 GB; reproduction is shipped as a Docker image that has to be ported to conda; no FP8 paths involved so Ampere is otherwise fine. Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/microsoft/SparTA/tree/pit_artifact .
reason: The sparse-kernel mechanism is per-GPU and Ampere-compatible, but the AE asks for 8xV100 or A100-80GB and 200-700 GB disk and ships as Docker, so both scale-down and a conda port are required.

title: ExecuTorch - A Unified PyTorch Solution to Run ML Models On-Device
note: PyTorch-native on-device runtime - memory planning, operator/backend registry, quantization workflows are all user-space and buildable from source. Concerns: most of the evaluation is on phones, NPUs and MCUs that are unavailable; only the portable/XNNPACK/CUDA backends can be exercised here
reason: Memory planning and quantization workflows are interesting, but the evaluation targets phones/NPUs/MCUs that are unavailable and the artifact is a very large fast-moving upstream project.

title: Laser: Buffer-Aware Learned Query Scheduling in Master-Standby Databases
note: Learned buffer-aware query scheduler; master and standby can be two DBMS processes on the same host. Concern: needs a full DBMS deployment and workload traces
reason: Buffer-aware learned scheduling is a real policy question, but it needs a full master/standby DBMS deployment plus workload traces to reproduce.

title: Massive-Scale Out-Of-Core UMAP on the GPU
note: Out-of-core GPU UMAP with an explicit single-GPU result (22.7x); batching/spilling strategy is the contribution and is squarely user-space CUDA. Concerns: multi-GPU is optional but is where the headline 74x comes from and the largest datasets exceed the ~257 GB free on /home so scale-down is needed
reason: Out-of-core batching/spilling on one GPU is a real memory-hierarchy question, but the artifact is the huge cuML upstream tree and the biggest datasets exceed local disk.

title: SpaceExit: Enabling Efficient Adaptive Computing in Space with Early Exits
note: Early-exit adaptive inference plus resource scheduling for satellite imagery; the artifact lists an ordinary CUDA GPU (tested on RTX 4090) and a multi-core CPU. Concern: the paper also uses a Jetson Orin Nano testbed emulating CubeSat hardware that cannot be reproduced
reason: The early-exit plus scheduling core runs on an ordinary CUDA GPU, but the Jetson/CubeSat testbed half cannot be reproduced and the satellite framing limits OS relevance.

title: ArrayMorph: Optimizing Hyperslab Queries on the Cloud for Machine Learning Pipelines
note: Cost-based planner choosing chunked reads vs byte-range reads for array data. Concern: targets S3 and Azure - MinIO substitution is needed and the cloud cost model will not transfer
reason: A cost-based chunked-vs-byte-range read planner is real I/O work, but it targets S3/Azure so MinIO substitution is needed and the cloud cost model does not transfer.

title: Heron: Automatically Constrained High-Performance Library Generation for Deep Learning Accelerators
note: Constrained auto-scheduling for tensor libraries - supports NVIDIA tensor-core GPUs and CPUs; concern part of the evaluation uses a Cambricon accelerator we do not have
reason: Tensor-library auto-scheduling works on our Ampere GPU, but part of the evaluation needs a Cambricon accelerator and search-based tuning is expensive in a 10-week budget.

title: Slapo: A Schedule Language for Progressive Optimization of Large Deep Learning Model Training
note: Schedule language decoupling PyTorch model definition from optimization. Concern - 3D-parallelism results need many GPUs; single-GPU primitives (kernel replacement, activation checkpointing) are still evaluable. Artifact repo is chhzh123/slapo-artifact.
reason: Single-GPU schedule primitives are evaluable, but the paper's headline 3D-parallelism results need many GPUs and the main repo is not the artifact repo.

title: AQD: Online Adaptive Query Dispatcher for HTAP Databases
note: Learned online query dispatcher that routes queries between row and column engines with low latency. Concern: needs an HTAP dual-engine deployment
reason: Query routing is scheduling-flavored, but it requires standing up a dual-engine HTAP deployment and the learned dispatcher is a DB-tuning contribution.

title: Hydro: Surrogate-Based Hyperparameter Tuning Service in Datacenters
note: Surrogate model scaling plus job fusion for hyperparameter tuning, built on Ray Tune; the Tuner half (model scaling, parametrization, fusion) is meaningful on a single GPU. Concern: the Coordinator half assumes a heterogeneous multi-GPU cluster with ephemeral resources and would have to be simulated or dropped.
reason: The Tuner half (model scaling, job fusion) runs on one GPU, but the Coordinator's heterogeneous-cluster scheduling — the OS-interesting part — must be simulated or dropped.

title: Dalton: Learned Partitioning for Distributed Data Streams
note: RL-learned partitioning for stream operators. Concern: built on Apache Flink - the distributed setup must be emulated with local task managers on the 32 threads
reason: Learned stream partitioning is load-balancing flavored, but it is built on Flink and the distributed setting has to be faked with local task managers.

title: EVT: Accelerating Deep Learning Training with Epilogue Visitor Tree
note: Epilogue Visitor Tree compiler for training-graph fusion built on CUTLASS; single GPU. Concern - CUTLASS templates were tuned for A100 (SM80); SM86 retuning may be needed.
reason: Single-GPU CUTLASS epilogue fusion is runnable, but SM80-tuned templates need SM86 retuning and the work is a DL compiler contribution.

title: WiseGraph: Optimizing GNN with Joint Workload Partition of Graph and Operations
note: GNN training framework with a joint graph/operator partitioning abstraction (gTask). The paper reports separate single-GPU numbers (2.04x) alongside multi-GPU, so the mechanism has a genuine single-GPU meaning. Concern - the largest graphs in the paper may not fit 24 GB, so a smaller dataset subset is needed
reason: GNN partitioning has a genuine single-GPU story, but the largest graphs will not fit 24 GB and the artifact is a research compute framework of unknown completeness.

title: CrossMapping: Harmonizing Memory Consistency in Cross-ISA Binary Translation
note: Memory-consistency primitive mapping in QEMU dynamic binary translation; QEMU TCG needs no KVM and no root, and the ARMv8-to-x86 and RISC-V-to-x86 directions run on our x86 host with PARSEC. Concern: the x86-to-ARMv8 and x86-to-RISC-V directions need ARM or RISC-V hosts we do not have, so only half the configuration matrix is reachable
reason: QEMU TCG needs no root and the ARM/RISC-V to x86 directions run here, but only half the configuration matrix is reachable and TCG-based PARSEC runs are slow.

title: RECom: A Compiler Approach to Accelerating Recommendation Model Inference with Massive Embedding Columns
note: Compiler that fuses massive embedding-column subgraphs for recommendation inference on one GPU - open source from Alibaba
reason: Open-source single-GPU compiler from Alibaba, but it is tied to an aging TensorFlow/XLA stack that may be painful to build against CUDA 11.8 and driver 535.

title: SEMA: A High-performance System for LLM-based Semantic Query Processing
note: Semantic query engine built on DuckDB with adaptive execution operator fusion and prompt handling for LLM operators. Concern: end-to-end numbers depend on LLM API latency and cost
reason: Adaptive execution and operator fusion over DuckDB is systems-adjacent, but end-to-end results hinge on external LLM API latency and cost, which this machine cannot control.

title: RALF: Accuracy-Aware Scheduling for Feature Store Maintenance
note: accuracy-aware scheduling policy for feature-store maintenance. Concern: paper runs on 800 cores, so the policy must be re-evaluated at reduced scale or on traces
reason: Accuracy-aware maintenance scheduling is a reasonable policy target, but the paper's 800-core scale means everything must be re-done in simulation and the repo's simulation path is unverified.

title: Diagnosing Performance Issues in Application-Defined Resources
note: User-space profiler (gigiprofiler) combining LLM semantic inference with static analysis, evaluated on MariaDB/Redis-class applications on one host. Concern: it "integrates with perf to sample hardware counters" - perf_event_paranoid=3 blocks that path, so only the instrumentation/LLM part is reproducible
reason: Profiling application-defined resources on MariaDB/Redis is plausible here, but the tool samples hardware counters via perf, which perf_event_paranoid=3 blocks, leaving only part of the system reproducible.

title: PipeThreader: Software-Defined Pipelining for Efficient DNN Execution
note: DNN compiler with software-defined pipelining, open-sourced inside TileLang; single-GPU by construction (FlashAttention, Mamba2 kernels). Concerns: the headline motivation is the Hopper Tensor Memory Accelerator, which Ampere lacks - the A5000 can only exercise the TensorCore/async-copy subset; also note the repo is the whole TileLang project, so the PipeThreader-specific code must be located within it.
reason: The headline mechanism targets the Hopper Tensor Memory Accelerator which Ampere lacks, so only a subset is exercisable, and the PipeThreader code must be located inside the whole TileLang project.

title: Experimental Analysis of Large-scale Learnable Vector Storage Compression
note: modular benchmark of 14 embedding-compression methods. Concern: full recommender datasets are large, scale-down likely needed. Merge note: scout linked the subdirectory https://github.com/HugoZHL/Hetu/tree/embedmem/tools/EmbeddingMemoryCompression .
reason: Modular embedding-compression benchmark is a memory-footprint study with a real repo, but recommender datasets are large and the framing is ML-accuracy-heavy.

title: Cocktailer: Analyzing and Optimizing Dynamic Control Flow in Deep Learning
note: DNN compiler that schedules control flow into accelerator kernels; evaluated on a single GPU. CUDA toolchain installable per-user via conda. Concern: the artifact pins a specific CUDA/TVM/ROCm stack and driver 535 caps the native CUDA version at 12.2, so toolchain pinning is the main build risk. Zenodo mirror: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7856472 . Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/microsoft/nnfusion/tree/cocktailer_artifact .
reason: Single-GPU DNN compiler with a Zenodo artifact, but the pinned CUDA/TVM stack against driver 535 is a real build risk and control-flow compilation is compiler rather than OS work.

title: ExoFlow: A Universal Workflow System for Exactly-Once DAGs
note: User-space workflow runtime built on Ray; the contribution (decoupling recovery from execution via task annotations and references) is a runtime design that Ray can exercise with multiple processes on one host. Concern: the paper's evaluation uses AWS clusters and serverless backends, so the team would need to scale the workloads down to a local Ray cluster.
reason: User-space Ray runtime can be exercised with multiple local processes, but the evaluation assumes AWS clusters and serverless backends so results must be heavily scaled down.

title: Decentralized Actor Scheduling and Reference-based Storage in Xorbits: a Native Scalable Data Science Engine
note: Decentralized actor scheduling and reference-based intermediate storage for data-science pipelines. Concern: designed for a cluster but runs as multiple processes on one host
reason: Actor scheduling and reference-based intermediate storage can run as multiple processes on one host, but the system is designed for a cluster so the headline results will not transfer cleanly.

title: Efficient GPU Kernels for N:M-Sparse Weights in Deep Learning
note: GPU SpMV and SpMM kernels for general N to M sparse weights - pure single-GPU kernel work in the nmsparse_artifact branch of SparTA - concern - evaluated on A100 and the artifact uses Docker so it needs a user-space rebuild and retuning for Ampere consumer cards. Merge note: scout linked the branch https://github.com/microsoft/SparTA/tree/nmsparse_artifact .
reason: Pure single-GPU sparse kernel work, but the artifact branch is Docker-based (unavailable here) and was tuned for A100, so a user-space rebuild plus retuning is required before any improvement.

title: ConfD: Analyzing Configuration Dependencies of File Systems for Fun and Profit
note: ConfD's core (taint analyzer, dependency analyzer, state generator) is LLVM-based static analysis of file-system source code - it runs entirely in user space with no root and no mounted file systems, and LLVM/clang is installable via conda. Concern: several of the six plugins validate findings by running xfstests and e2fsprogs against mounted ext4/XFS instances, which needs root; those plugins could not be reproduced, so a project here would have to target the static-analysis side (e.g. extending to more file systems, improving false-positive rate) rather than the mount-based validation.
reason: The LLVM static-analysis core runs unprivileged, but the mount-based validation plugins need root, so a project is confined to analysis precision on file-system source code.

title: KPerfIR: Towards a Open and Compiler-centric Ecosystem for GPU Kernel Performance Tooling on Modern AI Workloads
note: Profiling implemented as Triton compiler passes (upstreamed into triton-lang/triton third_party/proton/dialect); instrumentation is intra-kernel clock-based, so it does not need perf or root. note: Tensor-core SpMM kernel with asynchronous pipelining and load balancing; single-GPU CUDA kernel work, Ampere supports cp.async and FA2-style pipelining. Concern: evaluated on an 80 GB A100, so the larger graph datasets must be trimmed to 24 GB

reason: Fully user-space with a Zenodo AE artifact and modest dependencies, but it is compiler fuzzing whose success metric (bugs found) is too noisy for a 10-week improvement hypothesis.

title: JoinBoost: Grow Trees Over Normalized Data Using Only SQL
note: In-database gradient-boosted tree training expressed in SQL over normalized data; DuckDB-based, CPU-only single node
reason: In-database GBDT in SQL over DuckDB runs trivially on CPU, but it is a query-rewriting/ML-in-DB result with limited systems headroom.

title: zkStream: a Framework for Trustworthy Stream Processing
note: Official artifact repo from the authors' lab, described as "the artifact accompanying our paper". title: SecretFlow-SPU: A Performant and User-Friendly Framework for Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning
note: Frontend compiler plus backend runtime that lowers ordinary JAX/TF ML programs to an MPC IR - a user-space ML compiler/runtime, exactly the ml-systems bucket. reason: Fully reproduced artifact that runs all parties locally, but the contribution is cryptographic MPC compilation and the WAN half needs root-level link emulation.

title: RT: Regular Types for the Streaming Shell
note: Overlay type system for shell stream programs; artifact appendix gives the GitHub repo, checking is CPU-only and user space, and the evaluation corpus is hundreds of public shell programs. reason: CPU-only checker with a public corpus and an artifact appendix, but a static type system offers only checking-speed or precision as an 'improvement', which is a weak systems hypothesis.

note: User-space regular-expression engine enumerating all matches with output-linear delay; C++ library, CPU-only
reason: CPU-only C++ library that builds easily, but an all-matches regex engine is an algorithms contribution with little OS-relevant extension space.

note: Data-subset strategy that accelerates AutoML search; pure Python CPU workload, small footprint
reason: Tiny pure-Python CPU workload that runs anywhere, but accelerating AutoML search by data subsetting has almost no OS-systems content.

reason: A released evaluation testbed runs easily, but this is a measurement/comparison study of ML-for-DB representations with essentially no systems mechanism to improve.

note: Time-to-accuracy comparison of full-graph vs mini-batch GNN training systems. Concern: several baselines are multi-GPU or multi-node so a single-GPU subset must be chosen
reason: A comparison study whose baselines are largely multi-GPU/multi-node; the released scripts are a harness, not a system to improve.

note: Multi-objective RL configuration tuning for Apache Flink. Concern: Flink must be run as a local multi-process cluster and throughput numbers will not match a real cluster
reason: RL knob tuning for Flink is ML-for-configuration rather than OS resource management, and a single-host pseudo-cluster will not reproduce the throughput numbers the tuner optimizes.

title: DOTE: Rethinking (Predictive) WAN Traffic Engineering
note: Deep-learning replacement for demand prediction in WAN traffic engineering - training and evaluation are entirely offline on released topologies and traces and fit one A5000 - Concern: the domain is network traffic engineering rather than core OS and reproducing the LP baselines needs a solver such as Gurobi
reason: WAN traffic engineering is outside the OS-course core, and reproducing the LP baselines needs a Gurobi license even though training itself fits one A5000.

note: Static race detection plus LLM-generated tests plus directed fuzzing for distributed concurrency bugs - the eight target systems run as local processes; no root, no special hardware. Concern - the LLM test-generation stage needs an external API budget or a local model.

reason: A cost-based query optimizer is data-systems work rather than OS resource management, and the scalability half of the evaluation is distributed over 16 machines and unreproducible.

note: Bayesian-optimization query-level knob tuner for analytical engines - ML-based system tuning. Concern: tuning campaigns are long-running

note: Framework that prunes and quantizes networks against application-level goals rather than accuracy alone - the optimization pipeline runs on one GPU - concern - two of the case studies are a commercial agriculture robot and an electric-cart simulation so the application-level feedback loop may not be fully reproducible

reason: Spark SQL configuration tuning via multi-fidelity BO is ML-for-DB tuning; running Spark in local mode distorts the very resource behaviour being tuned.

reason: Federated-learning client sampling is mostly an algorithmic contribution; FedScale simulation fits one GPU but rounds must be scaled down substantially.

note: holistic RL tuning across knobs, indexes and query hints on PostgreSQL. Concern: tuning runs are long

note: Adaptive mixed-precision LLM training policy; authors themselves evaluate with a pseudo-quantization proxy because they lack Blackwell, so it is GPU-portable. Concern: pretraining compute must be scaled to small models

note: self-evolving RAG-based LLM query optimizer - learned component inside PostgreSQL - concern: supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning of an LLM needs a small model to fit 24 GB
reason: Repo exists and PostgreSQL runs locally, but SFT/RL fine-tuning of an LLM must shrink to fit 24 GB and query optimization is explicitly a low-os_fit area.

note: Software FP8/Posit8 quantization-emulation library for Transformer inference and LoRA fine-tuning. Concern - Ampere has no native FP8 so numerics are emulated (which is what the artifact does anyway); the accompanying edge accelerator hardware results are out of reach.

reason: Single-GPU CUDA Datalog engine runs here in principle, but some datasets exceed 24 GB, the exact artifact branch is unclear, and the contribution is a query-engine data structure rather than OS resource management.

note: Topology abstraction (TAG) for composing FL architectures; the Python SDK data plane runs standalone and the docs state the control plane is optional for running SDK examples, so multi-topology FL can be emulated with local processes on one host. reason: An LLM-agent framework for kernel optimization is ML-methods work needing API budget, and the H100 baselines must all be re-measured on Ampere before any comparison is meaningful.

note: Sparse-convolution engine for 3D point clouds with a coded-CSR format and adaptive dataflow - single-GPU kernel work with released code - concern - point-cloud datasets such as SemanticKITTI are large and the CUDA code targets older toolkits
reason: Single-GPU sparse-convolution kernel work with released code, but it is a domain-specific ML kernel and the datasets are large with an older CUDA target.
